evidence_items.summary: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. This motivates a shift from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout. Conventional linear probing offers a direct way to read this knowledge but is limited to final-layer RGB features. Multi-cue detectors broaden the evidence base, but their designs introduce other tradeoffs: adaptation may compromise pretrained transferability, heterogeneous encoders complicate feature integration, and late fusion precludes intermediate cross-view interaction. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers-inspired framework that reads complementary knowledge from spatially aligned RGB and wavelet views within a fully frozen visual foundation. ReMoT employs staged joint attention to enable controlled local and global cross-view interaction, while learnable fusion queries progressively read complementary evidence across Transformer depth without writeback. ReMoT achieves 91.2% average accuracy across eight benchmark groups with 3,074 trainable parameters, attaining the highest overall average among the evaluated methods. These results support structured knowledge readout as a promising alternative to backbone adaptation. Code is available at https://github.com/yunncheng/ReMoT.
evidence_items.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection

evidence_items.summary: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. We evaluate five video generators using verified, case-specific checklists. Experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but greater proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, while strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding.
evidence_items.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation

evidence_items.summary: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. However, existing 3D medical multimodal models often suffer from uncalibrated autoregressive decoding and shortcut reliance on irrelevant anatomical regions. We introduce Radev, a decision-native multimodal model that integrates anatomy-guided visual compression, direct candidate prediction, and counterfactual confidence supervision. To bridge global context with fine-grained slice details, a frozen 3D encoder extracts reusable organ-level features, which are dynamically selected by the query to attend to 2D slice features within predicted anatomical bounds. The resulting compact visual tokens enable the language backbone to estimate candidate probabilities in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding. We further propose Counterfactual-Calibrated Training (CCT) to compare predictions under intact and intervened organ representations. CCT encourages confidence to decrease when removing target-organ evidence degrades decision quality, while penalizing excessive confidence drops under unrelated-organ removal. To facilitate rigorous evaluation, we construct CT-Verdict, a comprehensive benchmark spanning binary finding presence, multiple-choice questions, and ordinal severity assessment across both in-distribution and external cohorts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Radev significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both decision accuracy and confidence calibration, while generalizing robustly under distribution shifts. Project page at https://juntaojianggavin.github.io/projects/Radev/
evidence_items.title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration

evidence_items.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. A growing number of LLM context engineering (LCE) approaches automate the task by casting the LLM itself as the engineer that draws generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trials as context. Although these methods resemble how humans learn from experiences, it remains unclear when and how LLMs can engineer effective context from data. To answer the question, we first establish a benchmark composed of datasets with different reasoning patterns. We compared different LCE methods with different LLM families in 8B size, showing that there is no single winner for all tasks, even compared with simple baselines like chain-of-thought. Even when scaling model capabilities via more parameters or generation iterations, LCEs do not consistently boost existing performance. Across all datasets and models, the performance gains of LCEs are negatively correlated (r=-0.5, ple 0.05) with the diversity of the failure modes of reasoning trajectories. Investigating how LCEs work, we find that (1) the improvement in instruction adherence can explain some success of LCEs; (2) one major bottleneck is whether LLMs can extract effective experiences out of natively diverse failures. Through this study, we uncover the limited capabilities of LCEs in abstracting principled contexts from diverse failure modes and understand how LCEs work, providing guidelines for future work.
evidence_items.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers

evidence_items.summary: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these three brief review items against the original inputs to predict diagnostic labels and a handling action. Supervised training learns individual judgments while comparing label assignments across related cases. A second stage swaps one review item at a time, using the resulting audit feedback to refine review generation. On JudiBench, JudiAct improves request and answer Macro-F1 by more than 28 percentage points over its 4B backbone. Across nine public benchmarks, it outperforms state-of-the-art guards on the mean delivered-answer score in both pre-generation and post-generation settings, cutting MM-SafetyBench attack success from 40.78% to 25.30%.
evidence_items.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Reservoir models underpin field development decisions that involve substantial capital investment, yet their quality assurance prior to simulation remains a largely manual process. Experts inspect property histograms, production curves, and parameter files across three heterogeneous data modalities: spatial fields, well level time series, and tabular parameters. This workflow is time consuming, subjective, and structurally blind to defects that arise at the interfaces between modalities. Here we present a quality control framework that decomposes reservoir model inspection into four modality specific detection tasks, then fuses their outputs for integrated assessment. Four specialized algorithms each target a single data type: Isolation Forest identifies statistical outliers in well point residuals, a convolutional autoencoder flags anomalies in geological property planes, an LSTM autoencoder detects contextual anomalies in production time series, and XGBoost evaluates simulation parameter validity. Structured detection outputs are fused through a weighted scoring scheme into component scores, and a large language model guided by a domain knowledge base organizes the evidence and recommends a final quality decision in an evidence traced assessment report. All automated judgments are confirmed by a human expert. Evaluated on the 10 held out test sub-regions of the Baoqing-1 fault block model (partitioned from 50 sub-regions into 35 training, 5 validation, and 10 test) under a blind test protocol, the framework achieved a sub-region level final decision F1 score of 0.89 (9 of the 10 held out test sub-regions correctly decided, with no defective sub-region passing undetected), compared with 0.50 for the industrial rule based baseline and 0.67 for an end to end XGBoost classifier on the same 10 sub-regions. At the parameter judgment level, it achieved a defect detection F1 score of 0.90, reported as a secondary consistency metric.
evidence_items.title: A collaborative multi-model framework with large language model fusion for automated reservoir model quality assurance

evidence_items.summary: Computational reproducibility checks are essential to scientific credibility, yet few published papers are ever independently verified, largely because manual checking is labor-intensive and time-consuming. We tested whether an agentic large language model (LLM) could perform computational reproducibility checks at scale. We benchmarked computational reproducibility checks performed by an LLM analyst (Claude Opus running in the Claude Code harness) against results from expert-led reproducibility audits in the social and behavioral sciences and found that LLM accuracy was comparable to that of human experts. Agentic LLMs can now perform high-quality reproducibility checks relatively cheaply, quickly, and easily, putting large-scale audits within reach for journals, granting agencies, organizations, and individual researchers.
evidence_items.title: Automating Reproducibility Checks Using Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the agreement between bone age (BA) assessments performed by large language model (LLM)-based applications and BA determined by clinicians using the Greulich–Pyle (GP) atlas, as well as artificial intelligence–based automated bone age assessment systems (ABAAS), in healthy children. Methods A total of 105 children aged 5–14 years, without chronic disease or treatments affecting bone maturation, were included. Left hand–wrist radiographs were evaluated by two clinicians using the GP atlas (Clinician-GP) and subsequently assessed by ABAAS-BoneXpert, RAD Sherpa, SMR-BAM- and LLM-based applications (ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot). Differences (Δ) between LLM and other assessments were analyzed, and intermethod agreement was evaluated using Bland–Altman analyses. Results Of the study participants, 55 were female (51.9 %), and the mean age was 9.42 years. Mean differences between LLM predictions and clinician GP assessments were minimal, particularly for ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot. Agreement analyses demonstrated close concordance between LLM outputs and automated systems, with the smallest discrepancies varying by sex and platform. Overall, the observed differences between the methods were relatively small. Conclusions LLM-based applications can provide results highly consistent with automated systems and clinician-based bone age assessments when appropriate parameters, such as sex and the reference atlas type, are correctly specified.
evidence_items.title: Agreement of automated and clinician Greulich–Pyle bone age assessment with large language model applications in healthy children

evidence_items.summary: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Model (LLM) research makes it increasingly difficult to distinguish incremental refinements from true paradigm shifts. This review evaluates 22 of the most influential publications spanning nearly three decades (1997-2026), organized through a causal, chronologically anchored taxonomy centered on the author's birth year (1999). Beginning "before 1999" with how recurrent neural networks (RNNs) forgot earlier context (much like forgetting Chapter 1 by the time a reader reaches Chapter 9), we trace how Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks introduced a "bouncer" mechanism of forget, input, and output gates to selectively preserve long-term memory. We then examine how Word2Vec turned language into vector mathematics (king - male + female ~ queen), why sequential RNNs hit a parallelization wall, and how the Transformer's all-to-all attention weights launched the modern LLM era alongside a quadratic bottleneck. Next, we analyze why scaling parameters alone leaves capacity under-trained unless data scales equally (Chinchilla), how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) left alignment superficial, and how that gap compounded into adversarial jailbreaks and single-direction refusal subspaces (J-space), where instructing a model not to think of a restricted concept surfaces it much like the human "red ball" paradox. Finally, we synthesize the current state of AI (2024-2026), encompassing recursive model collapse, autonomous reasoning-model jailbreak agents, machine-speed agentic intrusions, and closed-loop recursive self-improvement (AIDE^2).
evidence_items.title: From Vanishing Gradients to Recursive Self-Improvement: Evaluating the Most Influential Papers in Large Language Model Evolution (1997-2026)

evidence_items.summary: Soundscape assessment in tourism-oriented historic districts requires linking auditory experiences to activities in historic buildings and public spaces. We developed a prompt-guided, large language model-assisted framework using social media reviews of Huishan Ancient Town, China. Task-specific prompts constrained soundscape screening, verbatim extraction, emotion and sentiment coding, and place identification, complemented by model comparison, manual review, BERTopic modeling, an attention–sentiment matrix, and spatial clustering. Analysis of 4301 fragments identified 27 topics. The mixed-sound topic comprising conversations, broadcasts, and music accounted for 45.57% of fragments; topic shares varied across time periods. The model frequently assigned calmness or enjoyment labels to fragments about spring water, rustling leaves, and some quiet conversations. Irritation labels were common in topics about phone or video audio played aloud and repeated loud conversations. The widely reported mixed-sound topic had near-neutral mean sentiment, while the less frequent playback topics contained a concentration of fragments coded as negative. The 2353 place-linked fragments covered 89 grid cells at the 25 m scale. Clustering the cells by their review fragments’ topic proportions yielded six groups. The resulting narrative topic profiles summarize reports linked to halls, ancestral hall courtyards, pavilions, and waterfront locations. Reviews linked to the same place also expressed different evaluations of reported sound events. The framework compares how reviewers describe and evaluate sounds across activities and places. These comparisons identify settings for on-site assessment.
evidence_items.title: Differentiated Soundscape Experiences in Public Spaces of a Tourism-Oriented Historic District: A Large Language Model-Assisted Study of Huishan Ancient Town

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Linguistic annotation is an important aspect of linguistic description in studies that use corpus linguistic methods. Advances in machine learning have made it possible to (semi)automatically annotate some basic linguistic features. However, three barriers have limited the range of linguistic features that can be annotated in corpus linguistic studies. First, earlier machine learning models relied on a narrow window of local context, limiting the development of automated annotation tools for linguistic features that require broader contextual information. Second, achieving reasonable accuracy required infeasibly large amounts of manually annotated data. Third, many applied linguists have had limited access to machine-learning tools and resources, making it difficult to develop automated annotation systems on their own. Recent advances in language technologies and the growing availability of supporting resources, however, have largely mitigated these barriers. In this paper, we highlight the ways that encoder large language models and generative (decoder and/or encoder–decoder) large language models can be leveraged for the automatic annotation of linguistic features, provide a concrete example study on argument structure construction annotation, and suggest future directions.
evidence_items.title: Using encoder-based and generative large language models to facilitate linguistic annotation

evidence_items.summary: Introduction and Definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare refers to computational systems that help with analyzing, interpreting, and applying health data in clinical practice, public health practice, research, and administration. The World Health Organization (WHO) defines AI as "the capability of algorithms integrated into systems and tools to learn from data". Early clinical decision support systems, such as MYCIN in the 1970s, demonstrated how computers could be helpful in medical reasoning.Body: Machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal models, and generative AI all fall under AI in healthcare. Image interpretation, clinical documentation, risk prediction, triage, drug discovery, patient monitoring, public health surveillance, and personalized treatment plans represent some of the applications of artificial intelligence in the field. For the technology to be clinically effective, it must be validated, incorporated into clinical workflows, and shown to produce meaningful outcomes. FDA-authorized AI-enabled medical devices are becoming more common in clinical practice, particularly in imaging specialties. Multimodal biomedical AI, foundation models, and large language models that could process text, images, laboratory results, and other health data are the focus of current research. AI tools undergoing research, devices authorized for clinical use, and technologies demonstrated to improve patient outcomes represent distinct stages of development and evaluation.Conclusion: Artificial intelligence may improve healthcare efficiency, clinical decision support, research productivity, and access to care. However, clinical benefits depend on rigorous evaluation and appropriate implementation. Potential risks include algorithmic bias, patient privacy concerns, unreliable outputs, and limited transparency. Human oversight and continued monitoring remain important for responsible implementation.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

evidence_items.summary: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the expert-perceived quality, usefulness and readability of responses generated by ChatGPT-4, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini to common questions about primary herpetic gingivostomatitis (PHGS). Methods: In this time-specific expert-rating assessment, ten questions were entered on 9 April 2026 into the free public interface of each model (one response per question and model; 30 fixed responses). Twelve experts in Oral Medicine and Paediatric Dentistry rated the responses blindly using the Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI) instrument and a four-point usefulness scale; the total QAMAI score was the primary outcome. Readability was assessed with the Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKG). Results: All three models received high ratings. Gemini obtained higher descriptive scores (mean total QAMAI 28.5, versus 27.2 for Copilot and 25.9 for ChatGPT), but most between-model differences were not significant after false discovery rate correction, and inter-rater reliability was low (single-rater intraclass correlation ≤ 0.20). All responses required a high reading level (mean FKG 11.1–13.5). Conclusions: All three models provided acceptable responses, but between-model differences are exploratory. Expert-perceived quality does not establish clinical accuracy, safety or suitability for caregivers, and these single-time-point findings cannot be generalised to stable model performance.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models of Artificial Intelligence for Herpetic Gingivostomatitis: A Time-Specific Expert-Rating Assessment

evidence_items.summary: In today’s dynamic manufacturing landscape, Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS) encounter significant challenges arising from unpredictable disruptions and growing demands for customization. Despite the fact that FMS scheduling issues as a whole have attracted a lot of attention, the scheduling of RFACs has received very little attention. To address this gap, this study employs the notion of the intuitionistic cubic linguistic fuzzy set to manage uncertainty and vagueness inherent in linguistic assessments. To optimize task scheduling efficiency, this study proposes artificial intelligence (AI)-driven fuzzy multicriteria decision making techniques to create an efficient schedule for RFACs. Novel Frank aggregation operators are developed to effectively process uncertain information within the fuzzy environment. Based on these developed operators, an advance AI-driven multicriteria decision making technique is developed to solve uncertainty in decision making problems. In addition an AI-enhanced TODIM method is developed to comparatively assess the performance of RFACs across multiple criteria. Comparative experiments with existing approaches demonstrate that the the proposed AI-enhanced fuzzy decision making models provide reliable and efficient solutions for complex scheduling and evaluation tasks in manufacturing systems, while offering improved decision-making performance under uncertainty.

evidence_items.summary: Uterine scar pregnancy is one of the emerging obstetric complications these days, most commonly in the form of cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP), which is linked to uterine rupture, uterine bleeding, hysterectomy, and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). However, early risk stratification is challenging due to the nonspecific nature of symptoms and the operator dependence of ultrasound interpretation and clinical presentation that varies considerably. This structured narrative review explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning, and clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to enhance CSP risk assessment. The review aimed to identify and summarize the clinical and imaging factors associated with CSP risk, evaluate the reported performance of predictive models, assess multimodal, explainable, and workflow-integrated CDSS approaches, and identify barriers to clinical translation. The objectives were evaluated based on predefined evidence-extraction indicators. Among the selected ML models, those with strong discrimination were defined by the combination of heterogeneous endpoints, small cohorts, or cohorts limited to a single center, as well as limited external validation.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Risk Stratification in Uterine Scar Pregnancy

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in art and cultural production, reviving the question of who creates a work and to whom it should be attributed. This article situates AI-assisted production within a longer history of challenges to the figure of the solitary author, from Roland Barthes’s “death of the author” and Michel Foucault’s author function to the participatory practices of digital culture. It argues, however, that the distribution of authorship does not by itself demonstrate the distribution of creativity. Drawing on accounts that define creativity through novelty, value and social recognition, the article treats authorship, creativity and agency as related but analytically distinct questions. It then distinguishes two ideal types of distributed creativity: intentional-participatory distribution, in which contributors knowingly exercise some creative control over a shared work, as in The Johnny Cash Project and This Exquisite Forest; and infrastructural asymmetric distribution, in which people, labour or cultural materials enter a production system without comparable awareness or influence over the outcome, as exposed by Aaron Koblin’s The Sheep Market. Applied to generative AI, the distinction shows that users may work with models intentionally and iteratively while depending on training data, annotation work and infrastructures that remain largely invisible. Rather than treating AI as either an autonomous artist or a neutral tool, the article describes human– AI production systems in which creative control, attribution and benefit are unequally distributed, and it argues that questions of credit, consent and fair compensation must be addressed alongside, but separately from, the question of authorship.
evidence_items.title: Distributed Creativity: Rethinking Authorship in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: In the course of an additional investigation campaign for Snowy 2.0, in situ direct shear tests were performed during an early construction stage to validate design parameters which had been, until then, derived from results of laboratory testing. Since the shear strength of pre-sheared discontinuities had been identified as a governing factor regarding the stability of the Power Station Complex, which comprises two large underground caverns, it was considered as indispensable to test relevant features also under in situ conditions. After potential shear features had been identified in the process of geological mapping of a construction tunnel, probe holes were drilled and OTV inspections performed to trace potential features outside the tunnel perimeter. Based on the OTV imagery and the determined orientation of an identified shear feature, a test niche was planned and excavated. Within the niche, two blocks (0.5 m x 0.5 m) were prepared and tested under multistage loading conditions. The tested shear feature, a slickensided bedding parting, exhibited a dip angle between 38° and 40°. The paper describes all required work steps for block preparation and outlines the test execution. The results suggest friction angles between 26° and 29° with negligible cohesion, consistent with expectations for pre-sheared features. The successful execution of these tests under challenging site conditions established a new benchmark for in situ shear testing and provided robust design values for the large underground caverns of Snowy 2.0.
evidence_items.title: In situ direct shear tests on slickensided bedding partings – new benchmark for testing

evidence_items.summary: Background and Objectives: Monetary and physical indicators can yield different assessments of forest-product trade recovery. We examine Russian sawnwood imports into China. Materials and Methods: Annual Base pour l’Analyse du Commerce International (BACI) data for 2017–2024 support fixed supplier groups, four baselines and detailed-product composition checks. Separate United Nations (UN) Comtrade calculations retain original quantity units and use records reporting both weight and volume. Results: From the 2019–2021 baseline to 2024, coniferous unit values, in US dollars (USD) per tonne, rise from 236.70 to 372.29 for Russia and from 385.48 to 392.32 for the matched pool. Russian tonnes retain 62.31% of their baseline, compared with 55.95% for the pool, giving relative retention of 1.114. With a 2021 baseline, the proportions are 74.06% and 75.90%, giving 0.976. In the broad 28-supplier comparison, relative unit-value growth remains 1.514 under fixed baseline product weights. On the same three returned Comtrade records, 2024 unit value rises 14.20% per tonne and falls 2.61% per cubic metre relative to 2021. Conclusions: Recorded unit-value gaps narrow, while absolute physical imports contract. Relative mass assessments depend on benchmark choices; fixed product weights affect the magnitude of relative unit-value growth in broad sawnwood.
evidence_items.title: Russian Sawnwood Imports into China: Narrowing Unit-Value Gaps and Benchmark-Sensitive Mass Comparisons

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Accurate density functional theory descriptions of layered materials require exchange–correlation approximations that remain reliable as the nature of interlayer bonding changes with thickness. Here, we use diffusion quantum Monte Carlo (DMC) to benchmark density functional approximations for bilayer, few-layer, and bulk arsenic. DMC predicts equilibrium interlayer separations near 3.4–3.5 Å for three bilayer arsenene stackings, whereas bulk gray arsenic adopts a substantially more compact structure despite sharing the same nominal adjacent-layer registry with one of the bilayers. This contrast reveals a nontrivial thickness-driven evolution from a large-spacing, weakly coupled bilayer to the compact, chemically bonded structure of bulk gray arsenic. Among the tested approximations, SCAN+rVV10 most consistently reproduces the DMC equilibrium structures and relative stacking energies, while LDA, PBE+D2, and vdW-optB86b generally favor overly compressed geometries and overstabilize the bulk-like A1B–1 stacking. Based on this benchmark, SCAN+rVV10 predicts a thickness-dependent sequence from A1A1 to A1B1 and finally to bulk-like A1B–1 stacking. The structural evolution is accompanied by a stacking-dependent closure of the band gap associated with increasing interlayer As pz hybridization. These results demonstrate that the accuracy of density functional approximations for arsenene depends on the interlayer-bonding regime and establish DMC benchmarks for describing its evolution from the bilayer to the bulk limit.

evidence_items.summary: Particle contamination remains a critical concern in medical and semiconductor industries, especially considering the COVID-19 pandemic, which has heightened focus on clean-booth systems. These booths, equipped with blower systems and high-efficiency filters, play an essential role in maintaining air quality by removing airborne particles. In this study, computational fluid dynamics simulations, using modified Navier–Stokes equations with a k-ε turbulence model coupled with a Lagrangian particle model, were employed to predict the performance of clean booths in controlling particle contamination. The effects of blower arrangement, exit size, and airspeed on particle concentration were evaluated. At an inlet airspeed of 0.4 m/s, the simulated booth-average particle number concentration first reached or fell below the reference threshold of 35,200 particles/m3 in approximately 12 and 30 s for the configurations with 100% and 65% blower coverage, respectively. The alternating-row configuration with 50% coverage did not reach the threshold within the simulated interval. At the common blower face velocity of 0.4 m/s, the configurations had different total supply airflow rates because their active inlet areas differed. The clearance results therefore reflect the combined effects of blower arrangement and total supply airflow. For the fully covered configuration, the booth-average concentration reached the threshold in approximately 7 s at 0.6 m/s and remained above it throughout the simulated interval at 0.1 m/s. These clearance times describe the booth-average concentration and do not establish ISO Class 6 compliance throughout the booth. The model’s accuracy was validated through experimental measurements using a SKY6000 particle counter, showing a maximum deviation of 12.5% in particle concentration at different locations. This study underscores the importance of blower arrangement and airspeed in optimizing clean-booth performance for efficient contamination control.
evidence_items.title: Clean-Booth Dynamics: Investigating the Impact of Blower Arrangement and Airspeed on Contamination Control

evidence_items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve tool-using large language model agents, but target performance does not establish whether a training advantage survives deployment changes. This critical review separates target scores, target advantages over a comparator, and changes in those advantages. A purposive evidence map contains one registered comparison from each of 183 studies, including 57 four-score contrasts; it is not an exhaustive or prevalence sample. The synthesis identifies five distinctions that change interpretation: absolute performance versus relative advantage, harness-specific versus general gain changes, comparator identity, functional versus compositional and interface holdouts, and success coverage versus repeated reliability. We connect these distinctions to explicit source comparisons rather than pooling heterogeneous effects. A 24-study source audit and a new source-only duplicate AI extraction of 16 key studies expose uncertainty in exposure, resources, measurement, and coding. The companion records provide the complete 183-study bibliography, all 57 current four-score contrasts, target-level data, and coding disagreements. Evidence supports training advantages in particular deployments, but no general retention rate or universal advantage of multi-harness training. Crossed policy-harness evaluations, controlled tool holdouts, and calibrated simulation-to-real scoring are proposed to distinguish the remaining explanations.
evidence_items.title: Transfer of Training Gains in Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Critical Review and Evidence Map

evidence_items.summary: 3D layout-controlled image editing gives users explicit control over object placement and camera viewpoint. In a sequence of edits, however, the latest image can lose the appearance of an object when it is occluded or leaves view. The target layout specifies where the object should reappear, while its appearance must be recovered from earlier observations. We introduce LayoutRecall, a multi-round editor that stores and reuses appearance in the local coordinate systems of 3D boxes. Box-Surface Latent Memory retains image latents on box faces and retrieves them along rays in the target view. Geometry-Aligned Memory Conditioning supplies the retrieved tokens to a FLUX.2 editor using target-view positions, shared box-local embeddings, and object-wise attention. A correspondence loss encourages the editor to attend to matching observations during denoising. We also introduce LayoutLoop, a multi-round 3D layout-controlled image editing benchmark with calibrated layouts and designed revisits. We conduct extensive experiments on LayoutLoop and real-scene data to verify the ability of our method. The project page is at https://ykchizs.github.io/layoutrecall.github.io/.
evidence_items.title: LayoutRecall: Preserving Appearance in Multi-Round 3D Layout-Controlled Image Editing

evidence_items.summary: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes. Confirmed generation results are linked to the corresponding asset states, story time, and reference versions for verification and reuse by subsequent shots. Hierarchical Collaboration isolates execution contexts by task, clip, and repair round, and uses hierarchical memory to organize this process across multiple sets. Across multiple benchmarks, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods and produces long videos with sustained cross-shot consistency under predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.
evidence_items.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation

evidence_items.summary: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-based evaluator scores. On VBVR-Pro-Bench (Xu et al., 2026), a 500-instance suite spanning five cognitive categories with symbolic ground truth, the agent receives the same first frame and prompt as the video model, with no access to ground truth, metadata or generation models, and one attempt per instance. Three closed-model agents (Codex with gpt-6-astra, Claude Code with Fable 5.1 and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, each more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Among 23 runnable open-weight models, the best, GLM-5, reaches 0.572, above all video models except the RL-trained one. Together, we show that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and a prompt, program synthesis is currently a substantially more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation. We further distinguish depictive programs, which navigate the image to recover a transferable scheme, from propositional programs, which operate on hard-coded values, revealing how visual reasoning unfolds in agent-written programs and what it implies for its nature of reasoning in general.
evidence_items.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models

evidence_items.summary: Interactive world models must generate video continuously while responding promptly to user actions. Real-time throughput alone leaves input latency unresolved: coarse generation blocks delay action updates, and generation after input adds work to the response path. We introduce ShowNow, a fine-grained speculative streaming framework that uses computation available during playback to prepare action-conditioned futures before input arrives. Single-latent commitment enables frequent decisions, while configurable preparation covers one to eight actions. We construct a matched multi-future dataset to train alternative continuations from a common state; shared-history tree execution and fused commitment make their preparation efficient. On a single H100, our 5B model sustains 480p generation at 16 fps with eight prepared futures. In ViZDoom, the complete ShowNow deployment reduces median input-to-display latency from 620 to 208 ms relative to the native-block SolarWM-FT deployment. Matched-policy experiments reduce restart empty ticks from 1.56% to 0.09% (94%) and improve on-time responses to action changes. These results establish complementary roles for fine-grained commitment and advance preparation, with measured trade-offs in visual fidelity and long-horizon consistency. ShowNow turns playback-time computation into responsive visual interaction. Project: https://github.com/showlab/ShowNow.
evidence_items.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models

evidence_items.summary: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens. Their tokenizer must therefore preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semantic-enhanced tokenizers may lose acoustic detail, whereas acoustic-oriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that makes language modeling harder. Unified tokenizers combine both, but representing acoustic detail and linguistic content within a single feature space can cause interference between the two objectives, and existing approaches typically align acoustic representations to fixed semantic targets from a frozen teacher. We propose Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization (BiSAT), a unified tokenization framework with separate acoustic and semantic branches aligned by a shared-index mechanism. This design learns acoustic and semantic representations in separate continuous spaces while producing a single discrete code sequence, and it jointly optimizes both encoders without relying on fixed semantic teacher targets. Based on BiSAT, we develop BiSAT-TTS, a zero-shot text-to-speech system comprising an autoregressive text-speech LM and a conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder. Reconstruction, downstream understanding, and diagnostic analyses show that BiSAT effectively preserves semantic and acoustic information in the code stream, performs well on in-the-wild and out-of-domain speech, and learns complementary codebook representations. The frozen-code understanding results also support its feasibility and potential for code-based reward modeling in reinforcement learning post-training. BiSAT-TTS performs comparably to state-of-the-art speech LM-based TTS baselines with less training data, further supporting BiSAT's effectiveness for speech language modeling. The audio demos are available at https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo.
evidence_items.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.
evidence_items.title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion

evidence_items.summary: A publicly available dataset of 62029 rank-23 schemes for 3times3 matrix multiplication is presented. Every scheme in it has its own rank pattern, an invariant formed by the ranks of the factor matrices of a scheme, so all schemes are pairwise inequivalent. The schemes were obtained by a numerical method combining gradient descent with alternating least squares and by flip graph search, and have ternary, integer or rational coefficients. Rank 23 is the best known for this format and is optimal for schemes with integer coefficients, but the number of essentially different schemes of this rank was poorly understood: the existing collections of Heule et al. and Mårtensson et al. contain many schemes that share only a small number of rank patterns (17376 schemes with 387 patterns and 15316 schemes with 568 patterns respectively). The dataset shows that the number of different rank patterns is much larger than previously known.
evidence_items.title: So Many Ways to Multiply 3times3 Matrices: A Large Dataset of Rank-23 Schemes

evidence_items.summary: Spatial arbitrage pricing theory (S-APT) extends factor models to allow returns to spill over between connected firms, beyond what common risk factors explain. In recent years, tabular foundation models (TFMs) have matched or outperformed tuned gradient-boosted and bagged ensembles on small and medium-sized tabular benchmarks. Although their predictive performance is strong, these models reveal little about what they have learned, which limits their use in regulated financial applications that require explanation. Internal representations are widely used to probe what neural networks learn and to measure similarity. In this paper, we use the frozen representations of four TFMs as a measure of financial dissimilarity in a spatial asset-pricing model of US equities from 2011 to 2025, and find that their estimated gains over a direct distance between the same disclosures become consistently positive once broad SEC filing data are included. This reframes tabular foundation models from black-box predictors into instruments for measuring economic structure, with immediate applications to peer selection, risk attribution and network-based asset pricing. More broadly, our findings suggest that the internal representations of foundation models, not only their predictions, deserve study as economic objects, opening a new line of research on what pretrained models know about firms.
evidence_items.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity

answers.takeaway: These are the strongest scoring-method examples visible in the supplied summaries. A complete answer would require the full documentation for every first-observed artifact, because many summaries mention results without exposing their grading rules.
answers.takeaway_zh: 这些是所提供摘要中最有力的评分方法示例。要给出完整答案，还需要查阅每个首次观察到的成果的完整文档，因为许多摘要虽提及结果，却没有披露其评分规则。

answers.counter_view: The feed’s category-composition check found no material multi-day pattern, and unavailable connectors limit coverage. The stronger reading may therefore be routine publication activity rather than a reason to change evaluation priorities broadly.
answers.counter_view_zh: 该信息流的类别构成检查未发现实质性的多日模式，而且不可用的连接器限制了覆盖范围。因此，更合理的解读可能是常规发布活动，而不是需要广泛调整评测优先级的理由。
answers.plain_chinese: 应根据自身实际风险审查新发布的任务专项测试包。Context Clash 涵盖编码智能体的指令冲突，MLIRBench 面向编译器推理，NetBench 则面向领域适应。在将任何成果加入内部测试套件之前，应检查其数据、保留测试样例、许可证和脚本。
answers.plain_english: Review newly released, task-specific test packages against your actual risks. Context Clash covers conflicting coding-agent instructions, while MLIRBench targets compiler reasoning and NetBench targets domain adaptation. Inspect their data, reserved test examples, licenses, and scripts before adding any to an internal test suite.
answers.question: What should someone building or evaluating AI systems do differently today?
answers.signal: In this captured feed, releases outnumbered updates, while benchmark and dataset observations had higher daily averages in the recent comparable window than in the prior one. Treat this as a larger candidate-testing queue, not proof of a field-wide shift.
answers.signal_zh: 在本次采集源中，发布数量多于更新数量；在近期可比时间窗口内，基准和数据集观察量的日均值高于此前窗口。应将其视为规模更大的候选测试队列，而不是整个领域发生转变的证据。
answers.takeaway: Do not replace existing evaluations merely because more benchmark and dataset records appeared. Select relevant releases, reproduce a small sample internally, and add tests only when they expose a meaningful gap in your current checks.
answers.takeaway_zh: 不要仅仅因为出现了更多基准和数据集记录，就替换现有评测。应选择相关发布成果，在内部复现少量样本，并且只在它们揭示出现有检查体系中的实质性缺口时才添加测试。

answers.question: What does today's evidence fail to show, and what would change the reading?
answers.signal: This captured feed does not establish benchmark quality, independent reproducibility, broad adoption, or a representative field shift. Public-attention observations were far fewer than evidence records, and only a small portion of tracked artifacts appeared through more than one source.
answers.signal_zh: 本次采集源无法证明基准质量、独立可复现性、广泛采用情况或具有代表性的领域转变。公众关注度观察远少于证据记录，而且只有一小部分已跟踪成果通过多个来源出现。
answers.takeaway: The reading would strengthen with independent reruns, stable comparisons across repeated measurements, checks for test-data leakage and data origins, corroborated use across multiple sources, restored connector coverage, and sampling designed to represent the wider field. Those elements are missing here.
answers.takeaway_zh: 若有独立复现、跨重复测量的稳定比较、对测试数据泄漏和数据来源的检查、多个来源相互印证的使用情况、恢复的连接器覆盖，以及旨在代表更广泛领域的抽样，这一解读将更有力。但这些要素目前均缺失。
